nd-2026-10-25-trump-s-order-to-split-the.title: Trump's order to split the MMR shot runs into measles outbreaks and a poll showing half of parents believe spacing vaccines out is safer
nd-2026-10-25-trump-s-order-to-split-the.angle: An executive order wants to break the combined MMR shot into three separate vaccines given at different visits. Measles outbreaks in Amish communities are spreading and people are searching for SSPE. The reporting questions: are single-antigen measles, mumps and rubella vaccines even licensed and available in the US, how many more visits would a split schedule take, and what happens to coverage during the gaps? KFF's poll adds a second point: about half of parents wrongly believe spacing vaccines out is healthier, so the order matches a belief people already hold.
nd-2026-10-25-trump-s-order-to-split-the.why_now: The fall 2026 KFF tracking poll came out Oct 20. The executive order is recent, and measles outbreaks plus SSPE searches are exploding this week.
nd-2026-10-25-trump-s-order-to-split-the.is_it_real: KFF is an independent pollster, and the poll numbers belong to KFF. What the order says comes from KFF's summary and has to be checked against the order's text. Whether single-antigen vaccines are available in the US is a question for the reporter to answer, not a fact stated here. The pregnancy COVID-vaccine finding (falling confidence, uncertainty about a false miscarriage claim) is from the same poll series and can be a secondary thread.
nd-2026-10-25-trump-s-order-to-split-the.primary_test: Text of the executive order; FDA's list of licensed vaccines (does a monovalent measles, mumps or rubella product exist in the US?); CDC measles case counts; KFF Tracking Poll topline and methods
nd-2026-10-25-trump-s-order-to-split-the.other_peg: Measles outbreaks in Amish communities in New York and Pennsylvania, and the SSPE search spike Trend Desk flagged

items.title: KFF Tracking Poll on Health Information and Trust: Fall 2026 Update on Vaccine Views
items.summary: The latest KFF Tracking Poll on Health Information and Trust finds about half of parents mistakenly believe spacing out vaccines is healthier for children, while confidence in many long-standing childhood vaccines is high across partisans. These findings take on new relevance following President Trump's recent executive order calling for changes in U.S. childhood vaccine recommendations, including splitting the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine—currently given as a single combined shot—into three separate vaccines across multiple visits.

items.title: Recently Released KFF Poll Shows Uncertainty Over Established Safety of COVID-19 Vaccines During Pregnancy – The Monitor

Separately, conversations about childhood vaccines frame vaccination as an individual parental decision.

items.title: KFF Polling on Health Information and Trust

nd-2026-10-25-medicare-s-new-rule-target.title: Medicare's new rule targets 'ghost network' provider directories, Part D low-income cost-sharing and PBMs, and it lands during open enrollment
nd-2026-10-25-medicare-s-new-rule-target.angle: Seniors are picking Medicare plans right now from provider directories that are often wrong. CMS has proposed a rule to carry out the REAL Health Providers Act (directory accuracy), along with PBM accountability and changes to Part D cost-sharing reductions for low-income people. The story: what the rule would actually make plans do, when it takes effect (too late for this enrollment season?), and how to check a directory yourself before Dec 7.
nd-2026-10-25-medicare-s-new-rule-target.why_now: Proposed rule published Oct 20; Medicare open enrollment runs Oct 15 to Dec 7; there is a public comment period.
nd-2026-10-25-medicare-s-new-rule-target.is_it_real: The Federal Register proposed rule is the primary document. It shows what CMS proposes, not that directories will improve. Comment deadline and effective dates need reading from the rule itself.
nd-2026-10-25-medicare-s-new-rule-target.primary_test: Federal Register 2026-21420 (proposed rule text, comment deadline, effective dates); CMS directory accuracy audits and earlier secret-shopper findings on Medicare Advantage directories

nd-2026-10-25-275-million-to-recruit-nur.title: $275 million to recruit nursing home nurses: what it buys, and whether Medicaid's state directed payments to nursing homes reach staff at all
nd-2026-10-25-275-million-to-recruit-nur.angle: CMS's Nurses for Nursing Homes program puts $275 million toward roughly 4,000 nurses. KFF's new brief traces how much money states send to nursing homes through state directed payments, and two Boston College CRR papers look at how Medicaid long-term care policy affects aide and nurse jobs and wages. Together they raise a question families care about: when public money goes to nursing homes, does it change staffing at the bedside? Payroll-based staffing data can answer it.
nd-2026-10-25-275-million-to-recruit-nur.why_now: The CMS initiative, the KFF brief and both CRR papers came out Oct 20 to 23, and the federal minimum-staffing rule is still in flux.
nd-2026-10-25-275-million-to-recruit-nur.is_it_real: The $275M figure and the 4,000-nurse estimate are CMS's own and come from a digest summary with no URL, so they need confirming at the CMS newsroom. KFF and CRR are independent analyses; their findings are not in the item text and need reading. The same CMS digest summary also mentions an unrelated ACA eligibility-verification proposed rule (CMS-9873-P), which should not be mixed in.
nd-2026-10-25-275-million-to-recruit-nur.primary_test: CMS Payroll-Based Journal nursing home staffing data; CMS program announcement for Nurses for Nursing Homes; KFF's state directed payment analysis; the CRR working papers
nd-2026-10-25-275-million-to-recruit-nur.other_peg: Status of the federal nursing home minimum staffing rule

The story is whether weight-loss drug coverage is spreading or being cut, and what employers are doing in place of coverage (prior authorization, BMI cutoffs, lifestyle-program requirements).

nd-2026-10-25-is-it-real-esmo-week-s-75-.title: Is it real? ESMO week's '75% response' and 'cuts risk 62%' cancer headlines, and the one release that actually shows people living longer
nd-2026-10-25-is-it-real-esmo-week-s-75-.angle: In one week, drug companies put out 75%, 77% and 79% response rates (J&J's RIPTAC prostate molecule, Rybrevant in head and neck, Lilly's ovarian ADC) and a '62% lower risk' (Erleada). The test: tumor shrinkage in an early, single-arm trial is not living longer. Only a couple of these releases report overall survival from a Phase III trial (sac-TMT's 25.9 vs 17.4 months; Ziihera's three-year survival). Sort each headline by phase, endpoint and comparator, and show readers how to read the next one.
nd-2026-10-25-is-it-real-esmo-week-s-75-.why_now: ESMO 2026 releases, Oct 22 to 24. OptiTROP-Lung06 was published in NEJM at the same time.
nd-2026-10-25-is-it-real-esmo-week-s-75-.is_it_real: Every number is the sponsor's own claim. The response-rate releases appear to be early-phase and single-arm, with no survival data; that has to be confirmed in each registry entry. The release that cuts 'risk by 62%' should be checked for whether the endpoint is recurrence or death or something else, and whether there is overall-survival data. sac-TMT's survival result is a Phase III hard outcome, but the trial population and whether it applies outside China need checking.
nd-2026-10-25-is-it-real-esmo-week-s-75-.primary_test: ClinicalTrials.gov entries for each trial (phase, arms, primary endpoint); ESMO 2026 abstracts; the NEJM OptiTROP-Lung06 paper

nd-2026-10-25-is-it-real-ai-beats-doctor.title: Is it real? 'AI beats doctors': RAND says headline benchmark scores hide where medical AI fails, mental health especially
nd-2026-10-25-is-it-real-ai-beats-doctor.angle: This is evidence for Trend Desk's existing 'AI beats doctors at diagnosis' TFM idea and should be merged into it, not run as a second post. RAND argues that an aggregate score on benchmarks like HealthBench can hide large differences between clinical areas, and it uses mental health as its test case. That is exactly the gap behind 'outperforms physicians' headlines.
nd-2026-10-25-is-it-real-ai-beats-doctor.why_now: RAND perspective Oct 21; Microsoft's 'AI outperforms physicians' study is trending this week.
nd-2026-10-25-is-it-real-ai-beats-doctor.is_it_real: RAND is independent analysis; this is a perspective piece, not new trial data. Its specific domain-level numbers need reading from the paper.
